title: Next Smaller Element
description_html:
Classic interview problem with no LeetCode number — original source: geeksforgeeks.org/next-smaller-element (last updated 15 Sep, 2025).

Given an array arr[] of integers, find the Next Smaller Element (NSE) for each element in the array.

  • The Next Smaller Element of an element x is the first element to the right of x in the array that is strictly smaller than x.
  • If no such element exists for a particular position, the NSE should be considered as -1.

Example 1

Input:  arr[] = [4, 8, 5, 2, 25]
Output: [2, 5, 2, -1, -1]

Explanation:

  • The first element smaller than 4 having index > 0 is 2.
  • The first element smaller than 8 having index > 1 is 5.
  • The first element smaller than 5 having index > 2 is 2.
  • There are no elements smaller than 2 having index > 3.
  • There are no elements smaller than 25 having index > 4.

Example 2

Input:  arr[] = [13, 7, 6, 12]
Output: [7, 6, -1, -1]

Explanation:

  • The first element smaller than 13 having index > 0 is 7.
  • The first element smaller than 7 having index > 1 is 6.
  • There are no elements smaller than 6 having index > 2.
  • There are no elements smaller than 12 having index > 3.

Approach

Monotonic increasing stack, scanning left to right: for each cur, pop while stack-top > cur and set nextSmaller[popped] = cur; push cur. Anything left on the stack at the end gets -1. O(n) time / O(n) space — each index is pushed and popped at most once.

Exact mirror of LC 496 Next Greater Element I (flip the pop comparison). Previous Smaller Element is the same scan run right-to-left. LC 84 Largest Rectangle in Histogram uses both directions at once to get histogram spans.
